We use Taylor's formula in the form

$$
f(x)=f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a)+\frac{{f}^{″}(a)}{2!}(x-a)^{2}+⋯,
$$

with $f(x)={2}^{x}$ and $a=2.$ 

Computing the required derivatives, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={2}^{x} \\ f(2) & =4 \\ {f}^{′}(x) & ={2}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ {f}^{′}(2) & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ {f}^{″}(x) & ={2}^{x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡2)^{2} \\ {f}^{″}(2) & =4(\operatorname{ln}⁡2)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the Taylor expansion is

$$
{2}^{x}=4+4(\operatorname{ln}⁡2)(x-2)+\frac{4(\operatorname{ln}⁡2)^{2}}{2!}(x-2)^{2}+⋯,
$$

which simplifies to

$$
{2}^{x}=4+4(\operatorname{ln}⁡2)(x-2)+2(\operatorname{ln}⁡2)^{2}(x-2)^{2}+⋯.
$$

We substitute $x=2.1.$ Since $2.1-2=0.1=\frac{1}{10},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{2}^{2.1} & ≈4+4(\operatorname{ln}⁡2)(\frac{1}{10})+2(\operatorname{ln}⁡2)^{2}{(\frac{1}{10})}^{2} \\  & ≈4.29.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{2}^{2.1}≈4.29.
$$
